summary: This sermon examines Barnabas as a model disciple-maker who faithfully invested in Paul through relational mentoring, not just information transfer. The speaker challenges the church to practice authentic discipleship by surrounding themselves with mentors, peers, and those they disciple, emphasizing that prominence does not equal importance in God's kingdom.
key_points: Barnabas was not Paul's sidekick but a mature disciple who mentored and recruited Paul
Barnabas demonstrated obedience through selling his property, interceding for Paul, and stepping out of the limelight
Christians should surround themselves with three types: mentors above, peers beside, and disciples below
Discipleship is relational and holistic, not merely transferring information
The cost of non-discipleship is greater than the cost of following Jesus
big_idea: True discipleship requires relational investment in mentors, peers, and disciples, and faithful obedience in small things can have profound kingdom impact even without prominence.
title: A SUMMER'S JOURNEY: Living on Mission
